new_browser_corpus.scope: One functional verification of the fixed 10,000-record corpus per engine. Exact unmodified product module, no added exports or timing instrumentation; this is not an additional performance repetition.

new_browser_ui.scope: Six real UI scenarios per engine using the final quick9 HTML/JS and actual boundary dataset. Every pageerror listener is attached before navigation. Controlled crypto overrides are limited to error and cancellation cases.

new_txt_independence_and_error_preservat.scope: The localhost-served real HTML with a local TXT file selected through the file input; every boundary module/data request is blocked. This verifies no boundary request is made. Opening the HTML via file:// is outside this test.

chromium_five_paired_runs.scope: Fresh browser context per run, localhost HTTP, fixed num64/supp64, module-only. Cold means empty application caches in that new context; OS caches/browser executable remain warm. Cold import and first success precede timed 10k loop. Product plus temporary decoder timing counters and cache-observation export; optional profiling is diagnostic, not a benchmark claim.

nominal_20ms_actual_http_delay.scope: The local HTTP handler waits20ms for each actual request before response headers. Browser HTTP cache hits do not enter the server and receive no added delay. No bandwidth, DNS or TLS simulation. Each completed variant has a separate raw successful-response request log.

limitations: Linux x86_64 native results only; Windows/macOS native tests were not run.
CLI uses hardware RNG and cannot pair input values or expose automatic supplemental word counts; fixed-corpus probes establish exact bits and counts separately.
Five-run medians describe this host. File cache was not evicted; first runs retained; no formal significance claim.
Single-record runs are short and hardware RNG dependent, with overlapping timing and RSS ranges.
Median peak RSS increases of 64 KiB in the fixed probe, 200 KiB in CLI 10000, and 128 KiB in CLI 1 are preserved in this report; memory improvement is not claimed.
Actual CLI 10000 uses the product default parallel batch path; deterministic probe is single-threaded, so their absolute timings are not directly comparable.
Packaging is official deterministic uncompressed TAR plus a supplementary equal-method DEFLATE9 ZIP; archive payload hashes checked.
The 4.647% gain is the fixed Chromium module workload, not a claim for whole-UI throughput or every browser/network.
Cold-first-run ranges overlap; no cold-start speedup is asserted.
No additional performance repetitions were added. New three-engine 10000-record runs verify behavior only.
The 64 KiB packing regression remains rejected; original 512 KiB data and cache entry limits are retained.
